title: Quota demarcation and soft-spill routing for plan tiers
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Implement a quota-aware routing layer that enforces tier demarcation (free, paid, enterprise) while allowing controlled soft-spill behavior under short-term pressure. The feature should prioritize enterprise and paid plans without hard-blocking free-tier traffic globally; instead, the system should gracefully degrade free traffic via admission controls, reduced model variants, and regional spill policies.

Motivation: Customers expect predictable behavior when their plan limits are reached. Current hard-deny behavior causes sudden failures for low-tier requests and poor UX for bursty workloads. We need a routing policy that preserves SLA for paying customers, keeps free-tier requests best-effort, and reduces overall tail latency and error amplification during capacity pressure.

Goals:
- Enforce plan-level priorities so enterprise > paid > free for compute & capacity.
- Maintain latency SLOs for enterprise customers when possible.
- Allow free-tier soft-spill using lower-cost model variants, batching, or delayed admission rather than immediate rejection.
- Support regional affinity and per-region quota accounting to minimize cross-region spill.
- Provide observability: per-tier throttles, soft-spill events, per-tenant quota debt.

Non-goals:
- Full billing/modeling of long-term quota reconciliation (out of scope for initial rollout).
- Complex per-tenant auctions or bidding for spots.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Admission controller component (routing-adm): centralizes decisions per request:
   - Inputs: tenant_id, plan, region_hint, model_requested, tokens_estimate, priority_overrides (support flags), current_quota_balance.
   - Outputs: admit | soft-spill | reject, target_model_variant, queue_delay_ms.

2) Quota demarcation: maintain a per-tenant, per-plan ledger (lightweight cache with eviction) that tracks rolling consumption and short-term credits. Ledger stores reserved_capacity and warm_pool tokens for enterprise/paid tiers. Free tier gets a small burst window and a longer cooldown.

3) Soft-spill behavior: ordered fallback strategies applied when admit would violate protected capacity:
   - Variant downgrade: route to cheaper quantized/short-context model variant (e.g., 8-bit or smaller) with transparency header.
   - Latency smoothing: introduce small, randomized queue_delay_ms (10-100ms) to enable batching.
   - Partial acceptance: admit lower token budget response (truncate max tokens) with structured metadata indicating quality trade-off.
   - Reject only when no fallback applicable or tenant explicitly opted out.

4) Regional affinity and spill routing: prefer serving in requested region if capacity available for paid/enterprise. If not, attempt cross-region paid/enterprise fallback before degrading free requests to local spill. This preserves latency for top tiers while minimizing inter-region egress for free requests.

5) Configurable per-plan windows and thresholds: runtime-configurable SLOs/quotas per plan via Console. Changes must support feature flags for canary.

API changes:
- Incoming request header additions: X-Redwood-Plan: <free|paid|enterprise>, X-Redwood-Tenant: <id>, X-Region-Hint: <region>.
- Admission response headers: X-Redwood-Decision: <admit|soft-spill|reject>, X-Redwood-Variant: <variant>, X-Redwood-Quota-Balance: <tokens>.

Data model (implementation notes):
- Keep ledger in Redis clustered with per-region shard for fast reads/writes; fallback to central Postgres when consistency window allows.
- Admission controller consults a cached view updated via streaming (Kafka) of quota deltas to minimize synchronous writes. Writes are batched to reduce pressure.

Operational runbook (short):
- If free-tier queue depth > threshold AND enterprise p95 latency increases: enable emergency soft-spill multiplier to favor enterprise.
- If cross-region spill > 10% of paid traffic: alert SRE to scale capacity in affected region.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for admission logic, variant-selection table, and ledger reconciliation.
- Integration tests simulating mixed-tier traffic at scale in staging (100k rps mix).
- Chaos test: kill a regional serving pool and verify soft-spill sequence and headers.
- Load test with synthetic clients to measure p50/p95 lat and token cost delta under soft-spill.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): internal canary tenants + 10 external beta customers; feature flag on Admissions. Monitor metrics for 72h.
- Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% of free traffic with soft-spill enabled.
- Phase 3: Full launch after two weeks of stable metrics.

Metrics to track (Dashboard names):
- routing.admissions.rate_by_decision (admit/soft-spill/reject)
- routing.latency.p95_by_plan (enterprise/paid/free)
- routing.token_cost.avg_by_plan
- routing.soft_spill.events_by_region
- routing.quota_debt.count_by_tenant

Acceptance criteria:
- Enterprise p95 latency degradation < 5% vs baseline during simulated pressure.
- Soft-spill rate for free tier reduces hard rejects by >= 80% in tests.
- No increase in customer-facing 5xx errors for paid/enterprise tiers in canary.
- Console shows per-tenant quota balance and recent soft-spill events.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How strictly should reserve pools be enforced vs. dynamic stealing at short time windows? (We propose small reserved pools for enterprise and paid, reclaimed after a small cooldown window.)
- Consistency model: event-sourced ledger (Kafka) vs synchronous Redis writes. We prefer event-streaming for performance but must handle short-term divergence.

Links:
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/quota-demarcation-soft-spill
- Spec PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4123
- Staging dashboard (read-only): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/soft-spill-routing

Notes: Avoid coupling with billing system for v1. Include a small reconciliation job to surface discrepancies but do not delay admission decisions on billing latency.
